pixelConvention: Native original raw/G11.jpg (8016 × 6993), x right / y down. Open source-bank vectors.
method: Native original banks reread on 2×–8× source-pixel grids. Shape-preserving vector guides define a +/-7px search corridor; original unblurred raster cross-sections are matched jointly to printed ink centres, using 5px along-ink averaging and continuity penalty 4. Matching is disabled where the other measured bank is within12px, blended to full matching at20px; narrow banks stay on their independently read centres. A vector-offset smoothing spline has <=0.5px RMS fitting allowance, without filtering the raster. Final source-native vectors use shape-preserving interpolation at <=1.5px. Acute paired-bank tips use directly measured source centres to avoid bank collapse. No raster blur, geometric bank widening, modern coastline or fitted ground movement. Pulau Buloh is separately source-traced as a closed component; its existing false mainland membership was checked before addition.
limits: 1937 revision / War Office1941 / AMS1944 remains an approximate temporal substitution for1937–1960.

Blue mangrove hatch remains land. Only printed paired-bank reaches become water; single-stroke drainage and ink-obscured source continuations are omitted. The Buloh west arm opens to Johore Strait beside detached P. Buloh. Its main-island bank and the island full printed perimeter are traced separately.
G11 ground registration unchanged:18 controls, LOO RMS55.45m / maximum108.58m. Bank tracing precision does not improve or bound external ground accuracy.

The narrow unresolved head curl of the lower west Kranji tributary, single-stroke western Buloh continuation and ink-obscured southern continuations are not widened; each trace stops at independently resolvable paired bank centres.
